mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals weakening consumer demand and rising recession risk, which increases the equity risk premium and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of > 2% RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals improving manufacturing activity and earnings momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of > 0.5% INDPRO acceleration (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals strong labor market momentum, which supports earnings growth and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of > 0.5% PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1,100,000 units signals weakening residential investment and consumer confidence, which reduces earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when HOUST < 1,100,000 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in CPI above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates and increases the equity risk premium, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
